rationale: Palou leads IndyCar by 110 pts with 6 wins/6 poles in 2026, won 3 street races this season (St Pete, Long Beach, Detroit) and has 5 career street-course wins; Kirkwood won the last inaugural street race at Arlington (FOX Sports 'Paddock Buzz', Aug 14), but a brand-new DC circuit of unknown quali character keeps win odds moderate.

Tiangong Ultra won the 2025 Games 100m under the autonomy 0.8 multiplier (21.50s) ahead of two Unitree H1s (22.08s), while Unitree H1 reached a 10.1 m/s record in 2026 (New Scientist, Apr 28) and 100m becomes fully autonomous in 2026; a record 666 teams/2,056 robots line up Aug 22 (Beijing govt, Aug 15) so model names are uncertain.

Dos Santos beat Warholm in all three 2026 clashes and holds the world lead at 46.48 (Brazilian Champs, Jul 26) vs Warholm's 46.61 meeting record in London (Jul 18), with Warholm topping the DL standings; head-to-head at Silesia Aug 23 (Diamond League).

Jefferson-Wooden (2026 SB 10.78, edged Richardson 10.78-10.79 at Pre) and US champion Richardson (10.77 WL) are the form pair, Hodge leads the 2026 world list at 10.63 but has not been confirmed in the Silesia field that Diamond League lists as Jefferson-Wooden, Alfred, Richardson, Thompson-Herah and Jackson (Aug 5).

Antonelli leads the WDC 219-169 over Hamilton (6 wins) and Mercedes is dominant, but five different winners in the last five races, Verstappen has P1/P2 in all Zandvoort appearances, and an 85% rain forecast on all three days (Lente Desportiva, Aug 14) raises variance before the Sprint weekend.

Antonelli leads the championship (219 pts) and Mercedes is the strongest package in 2026, but Monza favours Ferrari's low-drag engine (Hamilton's record 7 Monza poles, Leclerc home favourite per Lucky Rebel preview) and McLaren/Red Bull won recent Monzas.

Mercedes/Ferrari 1-2 in points with Antonelli 50 clear of Hamilton (F1 standings after Hungary), Hamilton won the Barcelona round in June; Madrid's new Madring (La Monumental 24% banking) is a total unknown that favours the strongest car (Antonelli).

Mercedes-rated-favourite model for Baku (Podium Prophets) and Antonelli's 50-point lead, but Baku is F1's most chaotic street circuit with SC/VSC in every edition, Leclerc is the lap-record holder (1:43.009) and Verstappen/his rivals get extra variance.

Lemma (2:01:48) is the fastest on paper, world champion Simbu (2:02:47) is the headliner and defending champion Kiros won 2025 in 2:06:06; 25 men under 2:10 make this wide open (TCS Sydney Marathon elite field release; The Running Week, Aug 14). Sawe and Yomif Kejelcha are not in the field.

Reigning world and Olympic champion Jepchirchir (PB 2:14:43, fastest in field) headlines, with Cheptai (2:17:51), Shauri and Aga leading challengers among nine women under 2:19 (Sydney Marathon elite field announcement, Jun 29); Sifan Hassan is not entered.

Ingebrigtsen won the European 5000m title in 13:15.29 on his return from Achilles surgery (Aug 10) and is the 2024 Olympic champion auto-qualifier, but Yihune (12:47.62) and Balew (12:47.73) lead 2026's world list well ahead of that form, and Hocker is reigning World champion.

18-year-old Yan holds the 2026 world lead at 71.74 (8th all-time, Xiamen) and won three straight DL meets (Paris 67.44), with Borge (65.00) and Vilagos (63.88) next on the season list and Kitaguchi (Olympic champion auto-qualifier) third in Paris.

Pathirage dominates 2026: world lead 92.62 (Rome, second-furthest ever by an Asian), CWG gold 89.75, ranked world No.1 with 7 wins in 8 meets (Daily Mirror, Aug 6), though the 8-man field is a single-throw lottery.

Lyles won US title 200m in 19.63 (World Athletics) and 100m in world-leading 9.79 (Jul 26; he pulled up with cramp in the 200 final but called it 'just cramp'), while Gout (19.67) and Bednarek (19.69) lead 2026's lists; Lyles is the 2025 World and 2024 Olympic 200m champion and auto-qualified.
